content: The provided text is a detailed guideline for the treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB), including specific dosing regimens for various medications based on patient weight and age. 1. Dosage Guidelines for MDR-TB and RR-TB Treatment The dosages for medications used in the treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) were established by the guideline development groups for the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines on drug-resistant tuberculosis treatment (2018 and 2020 updates). These dosages are based on the latest reviews and best practices in MDR/RR-TB treatment. For certain agents, the dosages were informed by pharmacokinetic modeling results, which utilized the principle of allometric scaling to account for size and maturity differences in pharmacokinetics. 2. Pharmacokinetic Considerations Due to the pharmacokinetic properties of certain medicines, the proposed doses may exceed the mg/kg/day ranges shown in the guidelines to achieve blood concentrations similar to target levels in an average adult patient. For patients weighing less than 30 kg, the dosing schedule for those under 15 years of age should be followed unless otherwise indicated. 3. Weight-Based Dosing If multiple dose options are provided for a specific weight band, the lower or higher option should be selected based on whether the patient is at the lower or higher limit of the body weight range. Dosing should aim to closely match the target mg/kg/day, which is more feasible with oral or parenteral fluids and when solid forms of different dosages are available. Fractioning tablets into halves or smaller portions should be avoided whenever possible. 4. Therapeutic Drug Monitoring Therapeutic drug monitoring is recommended when the dose is at the upper or lower ends of the range to minimize adverse therapeutic consequences of overor under-exposure. This is particularly important for injectable agents, linezolid, and fluoroquinolones. 5. Special Considerations for Clinicians Clinicians may decide to exceed the recommended values in specific cases to improve therapeutic outcomes. For example, in individuals weighing more than 44 kg, a dose of 600 mg once daily may be proposed. Dissolving tablets in 10 mL of water may facilitate administration in patients in lower weight bands and avoid fractioning solid formulations, although bioavailability may be uncertain. The use of dispersible tablets is preferred if available. 6. Specific Medication Guidelines Linezolid: For dosing in the BPaL regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid), refer to the specific section in the guidelines. Clofazimine: Available in 50 mg and 100 mg capsules or tablets. Cycloserine or Terizidone: Dosage ranges from 10–15 mg/kg, with 250 mg capsules commonly used. Ethambutol: Dosage ranges from 15–25 mg/kg, with 400 mg tablets available. Delamanid: Administered as 50 mg tablets twice daily. Pyrazinamide: Dosage ranges from 20–30 mg/kg, with 400 mg and 500 mg tablets available. Imipenem-Cilastatin: Administered as 500 mg + 500 mg powder for injection, to be used with clavulanic acid. Meropenem: Administered as 1 g powder for injection, to be used with clavulanic acid. Streptomycin: Dosage ranges from 12–18 mg/kg, with 1 g powder for injection available. Ethionamide or Prothionamide: Dosage ranges from 15–20 mg/kg, with 250 mg tablets available. Isoniazid: Standard dose ranges from 4–6 mg/kg, with 300 mg tablets available. High-dose isoniazid (15–20 mg/kg) is also used in specific cases. Clavulanic Acid: Administered as part of a fixed-dose combination with amoxicillin (500 mg/125 mg). Gatifloxacin: Currently unavailable on the market and not used in individuals under 18 years of age. Pretomanid: Used only as part of the BPaL regimen, in combination with bedaquiline and linezolid. 7. Age-Specific Recommendations For patients under 15 years of age, follow the separate dose schedule provided in the guidelines. For patients over 14 years of age, use the adult dosing schedule unless otherwise indicated. Pretomanid is recommended only as part of the BPaL regimen and should not be used in isolation. 8. Administration Notes Medications such as amoxicillin/clavulanic acid are recommended only as companion agents. Fractioning of tablets should be avoided to ensure consistent dosing and bioavailability. Injectable agents like streptomycin may require dilution, and the volume may vary depending on the preparation. For intravenous use, the volume of administration may be increased as needed. 9. Future Availability Certain medications, such as dispersible tablets, are expected to become available in the near future to facilitate administration in pediatric and low-weight patients. 10. Special Populations In children aged 3–5 years, the use of half a 50 mg adult tablet of delamanid does not achieve the same blood levels observed in trials using the 25 mg pediatric tablet. Splitting, crushing, or dissolving the 50 mg tablet may further alter bioavailability. For patients weighing more than 30 kg, follow the adult dosing schedule unless otherwise indicated.
